text:
jaya (Support): Customer on Dedicated Private (VPC) in eu-west-1 reporting intermittent TLS handshake failures when traffic originates from us-west-2. Errors show up as 'tls: handshake failure' and occasional 502/504 with x-redwood-error: upstream-unreachable. Same service works fine when run inside eu-west-1. Can infra/networking take a look?

deploy-bot: deployment redwood/private-api-v2 succeeded in eu-west-1 at 2025-10-16T14:02:10Z

marco (Infra): do we have customer VPC association details? from experience this smells like split-horizon / private hosted zone not associated with all VPCs, or egress being blocked/translated to disallowed IPs. Can you paste curl + dig outputs?

jaya (Support): pasting minimal repro from customer (they ran these from an EC2 in us-west-2):
```
$ curl -v https://api.private.redwood.example/v1/generate
* Rebuilt URL to: https://api.private.redwood.example/v1/generate/
*   Trying 10.2.45.12...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to 10.2.45.12 (10.2.45.12) port 443 (#0)
* ALPN, server accepted to use h2
* TLS handshake: Client hello
* TLS 1.2 connection using TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384
* Server certificate:
*  subject: CN=internal-loadbalancer.local
*  start date: Oct 10 00:00:00 2025 GMT
*  expire date: Oct 10 23:59:59 2026 GMT
* SSL: certificate subject name 'internal-loadbalancer.local' does not match target host name 'api.private.redwood.example'
* Closing connection 0
curl: (60) SSL: no alternative certificate subject name matches target host name 'api.private.redwood.example'
```

marco (Infra): thanks — that cert mismatch is the smoking gun for some connections resolving to an IP that serves the internal LB cert. Can you also paste the dig results from both regions? especially against the VPC resolver.

jaya (Support): dig outputs they sent (eu-west-1 resolver vs us-west-2 resolver):
```
# eu-west-1 resolver (172.31.0.2)
$ dig @172.31.0.2 api.private.redwood.example +short
10.2.45.12

# us-west-2 resolver (172.31.0.2)
$ dig @172.31.0.2 api.private.redwood.example +short
54.239.28.12
```
(also TTLs differ; eu-west entry TTL=60, us-west returned public IP with TTL=300)

sasha (Networking): ok that matches the theory — some resolvers returning internal private IPs, others returning public IP (likely the public A record). If the private hosted zone (PHZ) for api.private.redwood.example is not associated with the customer's us-west-2 VPC (or with a peered VPC that their us-west-2 instances use), then cross-region requests can hit the public record. Public IP is backed by a different frontend/cert and will fail SNI.

eli (SRE): additional angle: NAT/egress allowlist. If traffic is hitting our edge from their us-west-2 egress IPs and those IPs aren't allowlisted (customer firewall), we see intermittent drops causing 502/504. Combination of DNS variance + firewall allowlist + TLS mismatch explains intermittent failures depending on which resolver/cache used by the caller.

jaya (Support): traceroute from their us-west-2 host to 54.239.28.12 (public ip) shows asymmetric path and some hops with * for ICMP; they also have on-prem VPN -> us-west-2 -> peered VPC. snippet: 
```
traceroute to 54.239.28.12 (54.239.28.12), 30 hops max
 1  10.0.1.1 (10.0.1.1)  0.44 ms  0.24 ms  0.21 ms
 2  * * *
 3  52.95.112.1  12.8 ms  12.7 ms  12.6 ms
 4  54.239.28.12  13.2 ms  13.3 ms  13.1 ms
```

marco (Infra): actionable checklist: 1) confirm PHZ association for api.private.redwood.example includes the customer's us-west-2 VPC (or the specific peered VPC used by their instances); 2) if they rely on resolver forwarding, ensure inbound/outbound resolver endpoints are healthy; 3) recommend lowering DNS TTL during remediation so caches update; 4) ask customer to run `curl --resolve` test to force IP and check cert (quick repro). Example: 
```
curl -v --resolve api.private.redwood.example:443:10.2.45.12 https://api.private.redwood.example/v1/health
```

sasha (Networking): also ask them to confirm egress allowlist on their firewall: if they restrict outbound to a specific set of Redwood IPs, they must include the egress IPs used by their NATs in each region — these can be different per AZ/region. If they can't open wide, recommend PrivateLink / interface endpoint so traffic never leaves their VPC.

jaya (Support): customer ran the `--resolve` test against 10.2.45.12 and got a valid 200/OK when forcing that IP and SNI matched; when forcing the public 54.239.28.12 it returned the internal cert (CN mismatch) or timed out depending on region.

eli (SRE): immediate root cause summary we can give customer: "DNS split-horizon inconsistency where some resolvers return private A record, others return public A record; combined with firewall egress allowlist and cert SANs only covering the internal hostname leads to intermittent TLS handshake failures."

leah (Customer Success): proposed message to customer to close loop: short steps to fix —
- Verify Route53 Private Hosted Zone association includes all VPCs that will call the endpoint (including peered VPCs).
- If using resolver endpoints, verify forwarding records and health.
- Temporarily lower TTL to 30s and flush caches (then raise TTL after confirm).
- Ensure outbound 443 to Redwood egress IPs is allowed for all NAT gateways / egress IPs used in us-west-2 (provide list if they want us to).
- If network policy can't be relaxed, we recommend PrivateLink/interface endpoint to avoid public routing and SNI issues.
- Run these quick checks and attach `curl -v` + `dig @<resolver>` outputs + a short tcpdump if still failing.

marco (Infra): we'll also validate on our side — confirm that the internal LB cert only covers the internal name and ensure our docs mention the cert expectation for Private deployments. I'll add a note to the incident that customers with split-horizon must associate PHZs across peered VPCs.

jaya (Support): passing fixes to customer. Follow-up plan: ask them to associate PHZ with us-west-2 VPC, lower TTL, test, and then confirm. If they still see errors after that, we will collect tcpdump and SNI logs and escalate. Closing this thread once customer confirms. :thumbsup:
